title: Quorum store vs consensus log vs CRDT/LWW
description: Three repair models. Quorum is not linearizable. CRDTs do not settle TokenX.

cells.workload: Item access with tunable R/W. High availability writes at W=ONE.
cells.consistency: QUORUM is not linearizable. Conflicting versions need a merge policy.
cells.latency: R/W replica waits. Cross-AZ QUORUM is your p99.
cells.scaling: Hash ring. Hot partitions stay hot.
cells.failure: Hinted handoff + read repair. W=ALL unavailable under one loss.
cells.whenNot: Constrained multi-row ledgers or 'QUORUM means correct.'

cells.workload: Leader-elected replicated log for config, locks, or a small KV.
cells.consistency: Linearizable if you read through the leader (or read-index) under the protocol you named.
cells.latency: Majority round trip. Cross-region majority is a product choice with a cost.
cells.scaling: Does not scale write throughput like a partitioned KV. Keep the log small.
cells.failure: Leader election seconds. Dual leaders without fencing split-brain.
cells.costOps: Cluster membership, snapshot, and keeping the log off the application hot path.
cells.whenNot: Your click firehose, or using etcd as the TokenX ledger at payment QPS.

cells.workload: Concurrent updates that can converge without a single leader.
cells.consistency: Eventual merge. Not unique allocation. LWW needs a clock you trust.
cells.scaling: Good for presence, counters with merge, collaborative state.
cells.failure: Clock skew rewrites LWW winners. Tombstone/GC bugs resurrect values.
cells.whenNot: Spendable balances, exactly-once settlement, or any invariant that is exclusive rather than mergeable.

assumptions: A partition is a named cut: some replicas cannot talk. CAP is a per-operation policy (TokenX debit rejects without proven authority; labeled stale reads may continue), not a permanent two-letter sticker.
LWW clocks need a named timestamp source; wall clocks skew.
TokenX unique allocation is not an LWW merge.
